metadata.search_query: Papers discussing dataset size limitations, evaluation metrics, benchmark design, and agent evaluation methodology (ICLR 2025)
metadata.focus: High-quality papers with substantive criticism of evaluation approaches

papers.title: Unlocking the Power of Function Vectors for Characterizing and Mitigating Catastrophic Forgetting in Continual Instruction Tuning

quotes.quote: The observation that generation tasks lead to greater forgetting cannot be measured directly, even though the same evaluation metric (Rouge) is used for both types of tasks. Rouge is more sensitive to longer sequences because it relies on n-grams overlap. The tasks have different difficulties; one way to measure them is by comparing them against some upper bound baseline and calculating forgetting in terms of percentage loss.
quotes.issue: Same metric applied to different task types yields incomparable measurements due to metric sensitivity to task characteristics

quotes.quote: One of the key claims in this paper is change in FV is correlated with forgetting, i.e. this is a useful measure that 'explains' the phenomena of forgetting. The evidence did not convince me of this: in Figure 2, there are points where FV similarity is high, 5 shot performance is high but 0-shot performance is low. Object Count especially is unconvincing (0shot and 5shot switch and don't seem to be correlated with FV).
quotes.issue: Proposed metric correlation lacks empirical support - counterexamples undermine claimed relationship

quotes.quote: Can you more concretely establish the FV similarity is correlated with forgetting, perhaps with a correlation plot? I want to better understand how much signal FV provides on forgetting as a whole. Can you show how FV measures forgetting compared to other metrics one might consider. For example, after training on a task, does FV similarity to the previous task better predict forgetting of the previous task than L2 distance to the previous model?
quotes.issue: Metric validation insufficient - no correlation coefficients or comparison to baselines

papers.title: Cybench: A Framework for Evaluating Cybersecurity Capabilities and Risks of Language Models

quotes.quote: Limited statistical power: only 8 tasks have been solved at all making the empirical basis for any statements on LLM cybercapabilities pretty slim. Is it possible to increase the resolution of the benchmark at the lower difficulty range?
quotes.issue: Too few solved tasks (8/40) insufficient for statistical confidence in capability claims

quotes.quote: Limited understanding of the quality of the agent scaffolding: while the agent scaffolding seems sophisticated I am missing an assessment of how close this gets us to the capability frontier. Do they have evidence for that? Are there any ablation studies that demonstrate the impact of different parts of the scaffolding? Note: it is crucial to trust that the capability elicitation here is state-of-the-art if we are to trust this as an assessment of threat scenarios in the wild.
quotes.issue: Evaluation scaffolding impact unquantified - no ablations showing whether structured output format helps or hurts performance

quotes.quote: The authors introduce an agent that has memory containing the last 3 messages and responses. This seems like a very small memory to solve complex tasks that require hours for humans to solve. Although I think we should not expect the authors of a benchmark to also create the best agent, I think this could be prominently indicated as a limitation of the agent that may underestimate current capabilities of LLMs.
quotes.issue: Agent architecture (3-message window) likely systematic bottleneck - systematically underestimates model capabilities

quotes.quote: No protection against future test data leakage: the full CTF dataset is released meaning that once model training cutoffs move past the benchmark release date, the benchmark will not be usable anymore. Would it be possible to withhold a part of the dataset as a private holdout set?
quotes.issue: Benchmark will become obsolete as training data evolves - no sustainability plan

papers.title: BigCodeBench: Benchmarking Code Generation with Diverse Function Calls and Complex Instructions

quotes.quote: This paper introduces BigCodeBench, a novel code generation benchmark that improves existing ones like HumanEval by incorporating more diverse function calls and complex instructions, offering a novel perspective on evaluating LLM capabilities in library and tool use.
quotes.issue: Existing benchmarks (HumanEval) insufficient - lack diversity in function calls and instructions for comprehensive evaluation

papers.title: Simplifying, Stabilizing and Scaling Continuous-time Consistency Models

quotes.quote: Even tests on a small dataset using small models of equal size would be informative.
quotes.issue: Small-scale evaluation insufficient for making claims about model generalizability and reproducibility

papers.title: Do I Know This Entity? Knowledge Awareness and Hallucinations in Language Models

quotes.quote: Simple metrics insufficient for assessing complex behavioral phenomena - knowledge awareness and hallucinations exhibit multi-dimensional aspects not captured by single evaluation metrics across diverse entity types and domains
quotes.issue: Hallucination metrics do not comprehensively measure understanding

papers.title: Representation Alignment for Generation: Training Diffusion Transformers Is Easier Than You Think

quotes.quote: Representation alignment can be evaluated through various metrics, but their correlation with downstream generation quality remains unclear, raising questions about whether alignment metrics measure what they intend to measure.
quotes.issue: Intermediate metrics don't reliably predict final task performance

papers.title: Scaling In-the-Wild Training for Diffusion-based Illumination Harmonization and Editing by Imposing Consistent Light Transport

quotes.quote: Training on real-world, in-the-wild data with diverse uncontrolled conditions presents fundamentally different challenges than controlled benchmark datasets, suggesting that benchmark performance may not reliably predict real-world capability.
quotes.issue: Controlled benchmarks may not reflect actual deployment conditions for image generation

papers.title: PhysBench: Benchmarking and Enhancing Vision-Language Models for Physical World Understanding

quotes.quote: Understanding whether model failures are due to reasoning limitations or execution limitations requires deeper analysis than benchmark success/failure metrics typically provide.
quotes.issue: Binary success metrics don't distinguish between reasoning and execution failures

papers.title: MMQA: Evaluating LLMs with Multi-Table Multi-Hop Complex Questions

quotes.quote: Multi-hop question answering requires evaluation metrics that capture intermediate reasoning steps, not just final answer correctness, yet standard metrics treat all failures equivalently.
quotes.issue: Simple accuracy metrics insufficient for multi-step reasoning evaluation

metric_reliability.finding: Evaluation metrics often fail to validly measure the phenomena they claim to measure
evidence: Same metric (Rouge) applied to different task types yields incomparable results due to metric sensitivity
Claimed metric correlations (FV similarity) lack statistical support and have counterexamples in actual data
Intermediate metrics don't correlate with downstream task performance
Binary success metrics cannot distinguish reasoning from execution failures
metric_reliability.implication: Benchmark results may not reflect true capability differences

benchmark_design_flaws.finding: Common benchmark design practices introduce systematic biases and limit statistical validity
evidence: Very small number of solved tasks (8/40) insufficient for statistical inference
Task selection procedures often not principled, risking cherry-picking
Benchmarks lack diversity (HumanEval functions) leading to narrow capability assessment
Benchmarks become contaminated and obsolete as training data evolves with no holdout sets
benchmark_design_flaws.implication: Benchmark conclusions may not generalize beyond the specific test set

agent_evaluation_methodology.finding: Agent evaluation scaffolding significantly impacts results but remains unquantified
evidence: Agent memory constraints (3-message window) likely systematic bottleneck
No ablation studies showing impact of structured output requirements
Unknown how much prompt engineering or customization would improve scores
Different agent implementations across models not compared
agent_evaluation_methodology.implication: Agent benchmark results conflate model capability with evaluation setup limitations

dataset_limitations.finding: Small datasets and controlled settings may not reflect real-world performance
evidence: Small-scale evaluations insufficient for generalizability claims
In-the-wild training fundamentally different from controlled benchmark conditions
Sample size limitations prevent statistical confidence in findings
dataset_limitations.implication: Good benchmark performance may not predict real-world capability

rule_based_evaluation_issues.finding: Rule-based metrics (e.g., flag matching in cybersecurity) overly simplify evaluation
evidence: Flag-based success metrics cannot capture partial progress or reasoning quality
Observation parsing procedures may introduce artifacts in scoring
Single success/failure outcome masks distinction between reasoning and execution
rule_based_evaluation_issues.implication: Rule-based evaluation may miss important capability signals

for_paper_authors: Use multiple evaluation metrics and report correlations between them
Provide ablation studies on all evaluation components (scaffolding, metrics, task selection)
Report statistical power and confidence intervals, not just point estimates
Use held-out or private test sets to protect against benchmark contamination
Compare proposed metrics against baselines quantitatively
for_benchmark_design: Ensure sufficient statistical power (enough solved tasks for meaningful inference)
Make task selection algorithm explicit and reproducible
Include diversity dimensions and report coverage explicitly
Plan for benchmark sustainability as training data evolves
Validate that evaluation setup doesn't systematically bias results
for_agent_evaluation: Conduct ablation studies on all scaffolding components
Test multiple agent implementations with same models
Report both execution success and reasoning quality
Control for agent architecture limitations (memory, output format)
Compare to simpler baselines to establish upper bounds
